included: All active28 Lean modules and135 named MhfeProofs theorems

findings.title: The regeneration wrapper suppresses a failed translator and can publish partial outputs
findings.blockingReason: Blocks reliance on the advertised regeneration command as a fail-closed assurance gate; it does not invalidate the separately reproduced current mathematical artifact.
findings.reproduction: Run AUD-014-harnesses/pipeline_probe.py with the actual two wrapper/splice scripts and the supplied synthetic translator. The translator emits minimal partial Funs/Types, reports an error and unconditionally exits7. The unmodified wrapper and splice return0 and create Code plus a new manifest.
findings.expected: A nonzero translator status propagates and prevents downstream publication of a successful regeneration artifact/manifest. Full unfiltered diagnostics remain available.
findings.observed: The pipeline ending in || true suppresses the actual Aeneas failure along with grep's no-match status. The complete wrapper returns0 after the translator's known exit7, with its error diagnostic present and synthetic Code created.
findings.impact: A person or automation can mistake a failed/partial extraction for successful regeneration, especially when a new manifest is created from those partial files. Unsupported extraction input, interruption or output I/O failure are ordinary causes of a nonzero translator result. This is an assurance-procedure defect. The probe does not show that the full135-theorem suite accepts partial output, or that the current real translation is wrong.
findings.evidence: pipeline-probe.json: translatorExit7, wrapperExit0, diagnosticSeen=true, downstreamCodeCreated=true; inner-log SHA256 822787ad77f087bc476b6d6163f2acabf86555630e9a50e9381e8f2c66b7a391. Independent read-only challenge confirmed actual script byte identity and the complete workflow witness. Real Charon and both real Aeneas replays separately exit0 and reproduce Funs/Types exactly.
findings.recommendedFix: Capture the translator status without filtering it away, retain its full log, fail before splice on any translator failure, and keep an expected snapshot manifest separate from a newly generated manifest. Add the partial-output failure case to the regeneration command's regression controls.
findings.requiredVerification: A translator failing before output and one failing after partial output both cause a nonzero wrapper exit and no successful downstream splice/publication. A diagnostic-free successful translator still passes; the real pinned extraction still reproduces the reviewed hashes and proof checks.

findings.title: Six closure repairs contain handwritten adapters despite being described as type-only changes
findings.reproduction: Compare all eight R dictionary blocks with REPLACED-blocks.lean.txt and original Funs.lean, distinguishing an instance's method field from the generated lower-level method function it calls.
findings.expected: The trusted-base description names every handwritten behavior adapter. Only changes that retain the actual dictionary method expression are called type-only.
findings.observed: Six FnOnce/FnMut dictionary methods introduce new monadic lambdas: projection of (output,state), or reconstruction of (output,back newState). Only the two outer stack closures retain their direct generated method reference while changing the output codomain. The underlying generated method functions are retained unchanged.
findings.impact: The public description understates the manual borrow/callback-state glue that must be trusted and reviewed. No wrong active-path adapter behavior, lost callback update or false checked theorem was found; the manifest already exposes the replacements.
findings.evidence: Two source-first independent scopes confirmed the six adapters and two codomain repairs. Actual FnMut paths preserve the generated callback state; generated back functions here are identity. Exact full splice reconstruction gives156 E +10 T +8 R blocks.
findings.recommendedFix: Describe six handwritten callback-entry/borrow-state adapters and two codomain repairs, delegating to unchanged generated method functions. Preserve the per-block Rust/generated references and hash manifest.
findings.requiredVerification: Every one of the eight R blocks is classified correctly; trusted-base tables agree with Translations and the manifest. No numerical or theorem changes are needed for this documentation correction.

findings.title: The input table incorrectly says the newer specification changes no requirement
findings.affected: Artifact PROOF-README.md:15; specification diff98620cc..3d88078 in README.md and docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md.
findings.reproduction: Read the fetched origin/main diff against the explicitly proved specification commit98620cc. Compare the input-table parenthesis with the added disclosure permissions, leakage allowances and wallet-check restrictions.
findings.expected: Keep the dated proof target98620cc and distinguish unchanged core cipher/vector bytes from later security-model and allowed-disclosure additions.
findings.observed: The newer text permits qualified disclosure of generation trial outcomes/count and restricted duration, gives2^-136*n and2^-120 allowances, and adds phrase-filter restrictions/warnings. Calling this no requirement change is too broad even though the scoped cipher algorithm is unchanged.
findings.impact: Readers may believe the old proof target automatically covers new generation-leakage and disclosure rules. This code proof supplies only a functional cipher-component bridge and does not audit or transfer those new bounds.
findings.evidence: Read-only coordinator/specialist inspection of fetched specification diff; separate snapshot-scope-challenge.md. Current core arithmetic/domain/round rules used by the proof remain unchanged.
findings.recommendedFix: State that the core cipher algorithm and vectors are unchanged, while the newer specification adds generation-disclosure/security qualifications not proved by this artifact. Retain exact target and newer revision hashes.
findings.requiredVerification: The input table accurately summarizes both revisions and does not credit the code artifact with new leakage estimates or whole-game refinement. No proof-source change is necessary solely to correct this snapshot sentence.
